string-array.name: municipalities_array
string-array.item: Beijing is the capital of the People\'s Republic of China and one of the world\'s leading global cities. With a history spanning over three millennia, it serves as the political, cultural, and educational heart of the nation. Home to iconic landmarks such as the Forbidden City, the Great Wall, and Tiananmen Square, Beijing blends ancient imperial heritage with modern metropolitan life. As China\'s second-largest city, it hosts the headquarters of numerous state institutions and Fortune Global 500 companies, playing a central role in the country\'s economic and international affairs.

Shanghai is China\'s largest city and a global center for finance, trade, and innovation. Located on the eastern coast at the mouth of the Yangtze River, it has evolved from a small fishing town into one of the world\'s busiest ports and most dynamic megacities. The city is renowned for its iconic skyline, including the Bund and Lujiazui skyscrapers, which reflect its dual identity as a historic treaty port and a modern financial hub. Shanghai serves as the economic engine of the Yangtze River Delta region, contributing significantly to China\'s GDP and international commerce.

Chongqing is a sprawling direct-controlled municipality in southwestern China, known for its dramatic mountainous terrain and foggy climate. As the largest of China\'s four municipalities by population, it is a major industrial and transportation hub along the Yangtze River. Chongqing is famous for its hotpot cuisine, Hongyadong stilted buildings, and the Three Gorges Dam region nearby. It plays a strategic role in China\'s Belt and Road Initiative and the development of the western regions, with growing sectors in automotive manufacturing, electronics, and pharmaceuticals.

Tianjin is one of China\'s four direct-controlled municipalities, located in the northern part of the country along the Bohai Sea. With a history dating back over 600 years, it has long been a vital commercial and industrial port. Tianjin is famous for its unique blend of Chinese and Western architecture, visible in the historic Five Great Avenues area. As a major industrial and manufacturing base, it is a center for aerospace, petrochemicals, and high-tech industries. The city also serves as a key logistical hub, connecting northern China to global markets through its world-class port.
